record.title: fix: clear the advisories that fail the release audit

notes: diff is 4 files, all dependency metadata (sdk/gamehub-js/package.json, web/package.json + both lockfiles); no source, workflow, migration, auth or secret handling touched, so the change is a clean revert if it misbehaves.

Reproduced the release gate verbatim: `npm --prefix sdk/gamehub-js audit --audit-level=low` and `npm --prefix web audit --audit-level=low` both report 'found 0 vulnerabilities' (exit 0). js-yaml resolves to 4.3.2 and vitest to 5.0.0 in both lockfiles, matching the commit message.

Verified the commit message's central claim rather than trusting it: `npm i -D vitest@4.1.11` in an empty directory with npm 10.9.8 does fail with "Cannot read properties of null (reading 'edgesOut')". The 3->5 major jump instead of the patch line is therefore justified, not an unexplained escalation.
Ran the suites on the new trees: sdk 9/9 passed, web 37 files / 221 tests passed, `make lint` clean, `make check-offline-bundle` (web-build + bundle check) clean, `make check-contract` clean.

`UPDATE_KERNEL_VECTORS=1 npx vitest run src/games/realmguard/kernel` under vitest 5 leaves the working tree clean - the committed RealmGuard replay vectors the Go verifier reads are byte-identical, so the browser/Go contract is not silently drifted by the runner bump.

`npm ci` succeeds for both trees inside node:22-alpine (the Dockerfile's web-build base), so the new vite/lightningcss native optional deps have the musl variants the image needs; `npm ci --dry-run` also succeeds on the host.

Node floor rises silently: vitest 5 declares engines ^22.12.0 || ^24.0.0 || >=26.0.0. The repo has no engines field, .nvmrc, or documented Node version, and CI/release/Docker all use Node 22 (22.23.x), so nothing breaks - but a contributor on Node 22.11 or Node 25 will now hit an engine error with no in-repo signal. Worth a follow-up engines pin, not a merge blocker.

The structural cause is not fixed and will recur: ci.yml:43-44 blocks only on `--omit=dev` while release.yml:88-89 audits the full tree at --audit-level=low, so the next dev-only advisory again turns red first at release time. The commit message names this and ci.yml's own comment states it as deliberate policy ('raise it on its own change'), so it is out of scope here.

Two incidental prod-tree entries changed in web/package-lock.json that the commit message does not mention: the file: link '../sdk/gamehub-js' 0.5.0 -> 0.7.9 (stale on main; now correct) and @jridgewell/sourcemap-codec 1.5.5 -> 1.6.0, a build-time transitive under @emotion/babel-plugin. Diffed both non-dev trees against main: those are the only two, sdk has zero prod changes. Both benign relock artifacts.
No tests were added, which is correct for this change - the thing under test is the audit gate itself, and I executed that gate rather than relying on a new assertion.
